title: CST-128-S: capped shift testing with a sequential bit controller

claims.statement: For CST-128-S in proof.md, for every integer N >= 2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N), k=n+4 and B=128N. The algorithm tests candidates sequentially on fresh independent ideal DCP copies, rejects a candidate at its first minus result, accepts after k plus results, and halts with output 0 before any acquisition beyond B. It uses the exact linear-gate arithmetic and sequential bit controller specified in Sections 3-4. Unconditional full-secret success is greater than 29/32. All constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. All four bounds hold jointly on every execution branch for this configuration and the epsilon(n)=0 error model below. Total sequential work is T(N,s)=O(N n log2(n+2)), hence O(2^n n log2 n) for n>=2 and at most C 2^n n max{1,log2 n} for all n>=1 with an absolute C. This includes source acquisition, all bit operations, gates, exact decomposition, streamed circuit generation, addressing, initialization, reset, measurements, failed tests, cutoff handling and output. The uniform time envelope B_T(n)=2^n n log2 n has exact growth index 1.

All constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. All four bounds hold jointly on every execution branch for this configuration and the epsilon(n)=0 error model below. The guaranteed malformed-sample fraction is epsilon(n)=0 for every N>=2 and s. For the actual acquired count Q, floor(epsilon(n) Q)=0 may be malformed. Every requested next copy is rho_s independently of earlier copies and the workspace conditional on the earlier history; the source has no later access to delivered registers. Algorithm-created correlations are unrestricted. Under this promise the same success and all four worst-case bounds hold. No positive tolerance, behavior on malformed samples, or maximal-tolerance claim is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
